about: Project-written predicate cases shaped like fwcheck's PowerShell input; expected verdicts follow the predicate rules.

cases.name: scoped
cases.what: one TCP allow rule for the exe on 2000-2002 scoped to the WSL adapter's alias, unrelated rules beside it

cases.name: today
cases.what: a TCP rule and a UDP rule with remote Any, any port and profile Public

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: (no WSL-scoped allow rule)

cases.name: profile-default-allow
cases.what: a profile whose default inbound action is Allow

cases.name: profile-disabled
cases.what: a profile that is not enabled

cases.name: remote-any
cases.what: an allow rule for the exe with remote Any and interface Any

cases.name: udp
cases.what: a UDP allow rule for the exe, scoped to the WSL alias

cases.name: port-2000-other-program
cases.what: an allow rule on port 2000 for another program

cases.name: port-range-overlapping
cases.what: an allow rule for another program on a range that overlaps 2000-2002

cases.name: port-outside
cases.what: an allow rule for the exe with local ports beyond 2002

cases.name: non-wsl-alias
cases.what: an allow rule for the exe scoped to another interface

cases.name: mixed-alias
cases.what: an allow rule for the exe scoped to the WSL alias and another

cases.name: exe-case
cases.what: the exe named in another letter case is the exe

cases.name: address-scoped
cases.what: a rule scoped by remote address inside the WSL adapter's subnet

cases.name: address-host-and-range
cases.what: remote addresses as a host and a range, both inside the subnet

cases.name: address-outside
cases.what: a rule whose remote addresses reach outside the WSL adapter's subnet

cases.name: address-localsubnet
cases.what: a rule scoped by the keyword LocalSubnet

cases.name: address-wsl-down
cases.what: an address-scoped rule while no WSL adapter is up: its subnet cannot be read

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): P2: CARLA by address
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P2: CARLA by address
fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: (no WSL-scoped allow rule)

cases.name: alias-wsl-down
cases.what: an alias-scoped rule while no WSL adapter is up

cases.name: disabled-open
cases.what: a disabled allow rule for the exe open to any address passes

cases.name: outbound-open
cases.what: an outbound rule is not an inbound rule

cases.name: block-exe
cases.what: an enabled block rule for the exe: harmless for the Windows client, blocks WSL

cases.name: block-exe-disabled
cases.what: a disabled block rule for the exe blocks nothing

cases.name: bypass-scoped
cases.what: an allow-bypass rule scoped as P2 wants is an allow rule, and not a block rule for P3

cases.name: bypass-open
cases.what: an allow-bypass rule open to any address fails P2

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): P2: CARLA bypass open
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P2: CARLA bypass open

cases.name: no-p2-rule
cases.what: no rule for the exe at all: the Windows client passes, WSL has no way in

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: (no WSL-scoped allow rule)

cases.name: unreadable-filter
cases.what: an enabled inbound allow rule whose filter could not be read is not judged as passing

cases.name: tcp-by-number
cases.what: the scoped set plus a TCP allow rule for the exe whose protocol is given as the number 6, on 2000-2002 scoped to the WSL alias: the number is TCP

cases.name: port-list
cases.what: the scoped set plus a TCP allow rule for the exe whose local ports are the list 2000, 2001, 2002 scoped to the WSL alias: a list inside the range is inside it

cases.name: ipv6-remote
cases.what: the scoped set plus a TCP allow rule for the exe on 2000-2002 for an IPv6 remote range on any interface: not inside the WSL adapter's IPv4 subnet, so P2 fails

cases.name: udp-other-port-not-judged
cases.what: the scoped set plus a UDP allow rule on port 53 for another program, open to any remote on any interface: it names neither the exe nor a port of 2000-2002, so no clause judges it

cases.name: interpreter-allow-any
cases.what: the scoped set plus two allow rules for the client's base interpreter, Public, TCP and UDP, any port, any remote, any interface: P4 fails for each

cases.name: interpreter-disabled
cases.what: the two interpreter rules of interpreter-allow-any, disabled: P4 passes

cases.name: interpreter-block
cases.what: a block rule for the client's base interpreter, any port: block rules pass P4

cases.name: interpreter-scoped-alias
cases.what: an allow rule for the venv's interpreter, TCP 8000, the WSL alias: P4 passes

cases.name: interpreter-scoped-address
cases.what: an allow rule for the base interpreter, TCP 8000, any interface, remote inside the WSL subnet: P4 passes

cases.name: interpreter-case
cases.what: an allow rule naming the base interpreter in other letter case and with forward slashes, any port: P4 fails

cases.name: interpreter-udp
cases.what: an allow rule for the venv's interpreter, UDP 8000, the WSL alias: not TCP, P4 fails

cases.name: interpreter-other-port
cases.what: an allow rule for the venv's interpreter, TCP 9000, the WSL alias: not port 8000, P4 fails

cases.name: interpreter-unscoped
cases.what: an allow rule for the venv's interpreter, TCP 8000, any interface and any remote: P4 fails

cases.name: interpreter-outside-address
cases.what: an allow rule for the base interpreter, TCP 8000, any interface, remote outside the WSL subnet: P4 fails

cases.name: unbound-allow-all
cases.what: an allow rule that names no program, no service, no package and no Owner, any protocol, any port, any remote, any interface: P2 judges it (Any meets 2000-2002) and it fails, and P4 judges it (Any meets 8000) and it fails

cases.name: unbound-tcp-any-port
cases.what: an unbound TCP allow rule, ports Any, any remote, any interface: fails P2 and P4

cases.name: unbound-no-service-read
cases.what: an unbound TCP allow rule on 2000 whose service, package and Owner were not read: counted as naming none, so P2 judges it, and it fails (any remote, any interface)

cases.name: unbound-scoped-2000
cases.what: an unbound TCP allow rule on 2000-2002 scoped to the WSL alias: P2 passes

cases.name: unbound-other-port
cases.what: an unbound TCP allow rule on port 80, any remote, any interface: neither 2000-2002 nor 8000, not judged

cases.name: unbound-icmp
cases.what: an unbound ICMPv4 allow rule, ports Any, any remote: a protocol without ports, not judged

cases.name: unbound-tm-port
cases.what: an unbound TCP allow rule on 8000, any remote, any interface: P4 judges it and it fails

cases.name: store-app-owner
cases.what: an allow rule with no program but an Owner SID (a Store app's network-isolation rule), any port: not judged

cases.name: store-app-package
cases.what: an allow rule with no program but a package, any port: not judged

cases.name: service-rule
cases.what: an allow rule with no program that names a service, any port: not judged

cases.name: exe-name-elsewhere
cases.what: an allow rule for a program of the CARLA exe's file name at another path, any port, any remote: P2 judges it (a deliberate widening of 2.5, a FAIL only) and it fails

cases.name: no-profiles
cases.what: the scoped set with no firewall profile read: nothing says the firewall is on, so P1 fails (the rules are fine)

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): P1: (no firewall profile read)
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P1: (no firewall profile read)

cases.name: block-exe-wsl-alias
cases.what: the scoped set plus an enabled block rule for the exe, TCP 2000-2002, whose interface alias is the WSL adapter's only: harmless for the Windows client, and for WSL an explicit block that wins over the allow (P3)

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: CARLA block on WSL

cases.name: p3-other-program-only
cases.what: the scoped case without its exe rule, plus a WSL-scoped TCP allow rule for another program on port 2000: P2 judges it (the other-program widening) and it passes, but it is not one of 2.5's own P2 rules, so --for wsl has no P2 rule (P3)

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: (no WSL-scoped allow rule)

cases.name: p3-exe-copy-only
cases.what: the scoped case without its exe rule, plus a WSL-scoped TCP allow rule on 2000-2002 for a program of the exe's file name at another path: P2 judges it (the exe-name widening) and it passes, but it does not name the 0.9.16 exe by its path, so --for wsl has no P2 rule (P3)

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: (no WSL-scoped allow rule)

cases.name: exe-range-half-outside
cases.what: the scoped set plus an allow rule for the exe on 2000-2002 whose remote range runs from inside the WSL subnet to outside it, any interface: not inside the subnet, so P2 fails

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): P2: CARLA range half outside
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P2: CARLA range half outside

cases.name: exe-no-interface-read
cases.what: the scoped set plus an allow rule for the exe scoped by a remote address inside the WSL subnet whose interface filter was not read (an empty list): a failed read, not a pass

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): read: CARLA no interface read
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): read: CARLA no interface read

cases.name: exe-empty-port-value
cases.what: the scoped set plus an allow rule for the exe on the WSL alias whose local-port list holds only an empty string: no port was read, so a failed read

windows-client: fwcheck: FAIL (windows-client): read: CARLA empty port
wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): read: CARLA empty port

cases.name: block-exe-no-interface-read
cases.what: the scoped set plus an enabled block rule for the exe whose interface filter was not read: P3 counts it, since it may cover the WSL adapter; harmless for the Windows client

wsl: fwcheck: FAIL (wsl): P3: CARLA block no interface read

cases.name: p3-unbound-only
cases.what: the scoped set with its exe rule taken out and an unbound TCP allow rule on 2000-2002 scoped to the WSL alias in its place: P3 counts the unbound rule, one of spec 2.5's own P2 rules

cases.name: p3-exe-path-other-case
cases.what: the scoped set with its exe rule naming the exe's path in upper case and with forward slashes: P2 judges it as the exe's and P3 counts it (the path in any letter case)
